originality.rationale: Compared exact functional identities, not just shared quadratic forms. The 2014 additive-set theorem imposes a difference-set hypothesis not satisfied for the pair of square sets used here. The 2015 conjecture and 2016 arXiv paper involve one nonlinear function and do not classify independent F,G. The 2017 article has a broad necessary quadratic-plus-periodic lemma, with up to five independent character coefficients, not the exact three-dimensional sufficiency for coefficient and weight 6. A finite rank-17 certificate plus a descent eliminates all nonparity coefficients. Targeted published-finding corpus and online queries found no stronger covering claim. Search is not a novelty proof; unindexed coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: Originality inference is based on targeted searches and inspected mathematical statements; obscure, unindexed, unpublished or differently titled prior work might contain the exact classification.

value.rationale: The question is a natural weighted sum-of-two-squares arithmetic functional equation for the principal form of discriminant -24, of class number 2, in the classical Kátai–Phong program. The exact solution is neither merely the quadratic template nor an unmotivated finite slice: a nontrivial parity character survives, and the theorem classifies all complex pairs without multiplicativity or other regularity. It upgrades a general necessary periodic envelope to a complete exact three-dimensional solution space. The explicit finite certificate and infinite descent reveal why the mod-4 character is the sole surviving deviation. The scope is fixed coefficient six and no implication about wider D is claimed.
